summary.short: Italian data protection authority (Garante) decision of 10 February 2022 finding that US company Clearview AI unlawfully processed personal data, including biometric data, of persons in Italy. It orders a ban on further scraping and processing, deletion of data, designation of an EU representative, and a €20 million fine.
summary.long: The Italian data protection authority (Garante) decision of 10 February 2022 finds that Clearview AI Inc., a US company with no EU establishment, unlawfully processed personal data, including biometric data, of persons in Italy through web scraping of publicly available images and a facial-recognition search service. It holds that the GDPR applies under Article 3(2) and finds breaches of Articles 5(1)(a), (b) and (e), 6, 9, 12, 13, 14, 15 and 27; no breach of Article 22 is found. Operative orders: a prohibition on further web scraping of images and metadata of persons in Italy and on further processing of such data (Art. 58(2)(f)); deletion of that data (Art. 58(2)(g)); designation of a representative in the EU within 30 days (Art. 58(2)(d)); and a report on measures taken within 30 days. The Garante imposes an administrative fine of EUR 20 million under Article 83(5) and orders publication of the decision on its website. The decision notes the company may settle by complying and paying half the fine within 60 days; judicial opposition is available within 30 days.

relations.note: The GDPR is the regulation under which the proceeding, the corrective measures and the administrative fine are adopted.

notes: The text uses placeholder URLs (https://...) and redacted complainant identifiers (XX), so URL-level facts cannot be verified from the document. The EUR 20 million fine is the statutory maximum under art. 83(5) and is stated as applied; the breakdown (3.8 million for each violation of arts. 5, 6 and 9; 2 million for each of arts. 12-15; 600,000 for art. 27) sums to 20 million. Company submissions on jurisdiction and on its non-application of the GDPR are recorded as the company's position and rejected by the Garante. Art. 22 was not found violated. The decision allows settlement at half the fine under art. 166(8) Codice; this option is not coded as an event. The conclusions list arts. 5(1)(a), (b), (e), 6, 9, 12, 13, 14, 15 and 27, while section 3.6.4 states the violation of arts. 12, 15, 13 and 14 in one sentence.

thresholds.note: No numeric cutoff in the decision changes the legal treatment of a person or entity. The EUR 20 million and 4% turnover figures are penalty maxima (enforcement, not coded here). The 30-day and one-month response periods are procedural time limits. The two-requests-in-twelve-months limit is a term of Clearview's own policy. The 512-vector and 10-billion-image figures are technical description or company claims. The moratorium runs to 31 December 2023 and is recorded as a date.
